# 2 Samuel Chapter 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 180v–181v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_012_page_001.jpg, 2SA_012_page_002.jpg, 2SA_012_page_003.jpg

---

**12:1** And-sent YHWH Natan to David. And-he-came to-him, and-said to-him, "Two men were in-one city, one rich and-one poor.

**12:2** To-the-rich-[man] there-were flocks and-herds, exceedingly many.

**12:3** And-to-the-poor-[man] there-was-nothing except one ewe-lamb [kivsah], a-small-one, that he-had-bought and-sustained [yechayeha], and-she-grew-up with-him and-with his-children together. From-his-morsel she-ate, and-from-his-cup she-drank, and-in-his-bosom she-lay-down, and-she-was to-him as-a-daughter.

**12:4** And-came a-traveler [helekh] to the-rich man, and-he-spared [vayachmal] to-take from-his-flock and-from-his-herd to-prepare for-the-wayfarer [oreach] who-had-come to-him. And-he-took the-ewe-lamb of-the-poor man, and-prepared-her for-the-man who-had-come to-him."

**12:5** And-burned [the]-anger of-David against the-man exceedingly, and-he-said to Natan, "As-YHWH lives [chay-YHWH], surely a-son of-death [ben-mavet] [is] the-man who-does this!

**12:6** And the-ewe-lamb he-shall-repay fourfold [arba'atayim], because [al eqev] he-did this thing, and-because he-had-no pity [lo chamal]."

**12:7** And-said Natan to David, "You [are] the-man! [attah ha-ish!] Thus says YHWH, God of-Yisra'el: 'I anointed-you [meshachtikha] as-king over Yisra'el, and-I delivered-you from-[the]-hand of-Sha'ul.

**12:8** And-I-gave to-you [the]-house of-your-lord, and-[the]-wives of-your-lord into-your-bosom, and-I-gave to-you [the]-house of-Yisra'el and-Yehudah; and-if [that were]-too-little, I-would-have-added to-you like-these and-like-these.

**12:9** Why have-you-despised [bazita] [the]-word of-YHWH, to-do the-evil [ha-ra] in-his-eyes? Uriyah the-Chitti you-struck with-the-sword, and-his-wife you-took to-you as-a-wife, and-him you-killed with-[the]-sword of-[the]-sons of-Ammon.

**12:10** And-now, not shall-depart [the]-sword from-your-house until-forever [ad-olam], because you-despised-me [bezitani], and-took [the]-wife of-Uriyah the-Chitti to-be to-you as-a-wife.'

**12:11** Thus says YHWH: 'Behold-me raising-up [meqim] upon-you evil [ra'ah] from-your-house, and-I-will-take your-wives before-your-eyes, and-give to-your-neighbor [lere'ekha], and-he-shall-lie-with your-wives before-[the]-eyes of-this sun.

**12:12** For you did [it] in-secret, and-I will-do this thing before all Yisra'el and-before the-sun.'"

**12:13** And-said David to Natan, "I-have-sinned [chatati] against-YHWH [la-YHWH]." And-said Natan to David, "Also YHWH has-passed-over [he'evir] your-sin [chatatkha]; you-shall-not die.

**12:14** However, because you-have-utterly-scorned [na'ets ni'atsta] the-enemies of-YHWH by-this thing, also the-son, the-one-born to-you — dying he-shall-die [mot yamut]."

**12:15** And-went Natan to his-house. And-struck YHWH the-child that [the]-wife of-Uriyah bore to-David, and-he-became-ill [vaye'anash].

**12:16** And-sought David God [Elohim] for-the-sake-of the-boy [na'ar], and-fasted David a-fast, and-came and-spent-the-night [velan] and-lay upon-the-ground.

**12:17** And-arose [the]-elders of-his-house upon-him to-raise-him from-the-ground, and-he-was-not willing, and-not he-ate with-them bread.

**12:18** And-it-was on-the-day the-seventh, and-died the-child. And-feared [the]-servants of-David to-tell him that the-child [was]-dead, for they-said, "Behold, while the-child was alive we-spoke to-him and-he-did-not listen to-our-voice, and-how shall-we-say to-him, 'The-child is-dead'? And-he-will-do evil [vera'ah]."

**12:19** And-saw David that his-servants [were]-whispering [mitlachashim], and-understood David that the-child [was]-dead. And-said David to his-servants, "Is-the-child dead?" And-they-said, "Dead."

**12:20** And-rose David from-the-ground, and-washed and-anointed-himself [vayasakh] and-changed his-garments, and-came to-[the]-house of-YHWH and-bowed-down [vayishtachu]. And-he-came to his-house and-asked, and-they-set before-him bread, and-he-ate.

**12:21** And-said his-servants to-him, "What [is] this thing that you-have-done? For-the-sake-of the-child alive you-fasted and-wept, and-when the-child died you-rose and-ate bread?"

**12:22** And-he-said, "While the-child [was] still alive I-fasted and-wept, for I-said, 'Who knows [mi yodea]? YHWH may-be-gracious-to-me [yechanneni] and-the-child will-live.'

**12:23** And-now he-has-died, why [is]-this [that]-I [am]-fasting? Am-I-able to-bring-him-back again? I [am]-going to-him, and-he will-not return to-me."

**12:24** And-comforted David Bat-Sheva his-wife, and-came to-her and-lay with-her, and-she-bore a-son, and-called his-name Shelomoh. And-YHWH loved-him [va-YHWH ahevo].

**12:25** And-sent by-[the]-hand of-Natan the-prophet, and-called his-name Yedidyah [beloved of-YHWH], for-the-sake-of YHWH.

**12:26** And-fought Yo'av against-Rabbah of-[the]-sons of-Ammon, and-captured the-city of-the-kingship [ir ha-melukhah].

**12:27** And-sent Yo'av messengers to David, and-said, "I-have-fought against-Rabbah; also I-have-captured the-city of-the-waters [ir ha-mayim].

**12:28** And-now gather the-rest of-the-people and-encamp against the-city and-capture-it, lest I capture the-city and-be-called my-name upon-it."

**12:29** And-gathered David all the-people and-went to-Rabbah, and-fought against-it and-captured-it.

**12:30** And-took the-crown of-their-king [malkam] from-upon his-head — and-its-weight [was] a-talent [kikkar] of-gold, and-[a]-precious stone — and-it-was upon [the]-head of-David. And-[the]-plunder of-the-city he-brought-out, exceedingly much.

**12:31** And-the-people who [were] in-it he-brought-out, and-set [vayasem] [them] at-the-saw [bammegerah] and-at-[the]-iron threshing-sledges [bacharitsey ha-barzel] and-at-[the]-iron axes [uvamagzerot ha-barzel], and-passed-them [he'evir] through the-brick-kiln [bammalben]. And-thus he-did to-all [the]-cities of-[the]-sons of-Ammon. And-returned David and-all the-people to-Yerushalayim.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.3 — kivsah:** The "ewe-lamb" (*kivsah*) is a carefully chosen feminine form, corresponding to Bathsheba in the parable. The intimate details — eating from his morsel, drinking from his cup, lying in his bosom — use the language of marital intimacy.

**v.5 — ben-mavet:** "Son of death" is a Hebrew idiom meaning "deserving of death." David pronounces his own sentence.

**v.7 — attah ha-ish:** Three words that constitute one of the most powerful moments in biblical literature. Nathan's accusation is a devastating reversal: the judge becomes the judged.

**v.13 — chatati la-YHWH:** David's confession is strikingly brief — three words in Hebrew: חָטָאתִי לַיהוָה. The preposition *la-* indicates the direction of the sin: against YHWH. David does not mention Bathsheba or Uriah by name.

**v.14 — na'ets ni'atsta:** The infinitive absolute construction "scorning you have scorned" intensifies the verb. The MT reads "the enemies of YHWH" (*oyevey YHWH*), which is widely recognized as a scribal euphemism (tiqqun soferim) to avoid saying David scorned YHWH directly.

**v.23 — ani holekh elav:** "I am going to him" — one of the most poignant statements about death and the afterlife in the Hebrew Bible. David accepts the finality of death while expressing a hope (or at least a resignation) that he will join his son in Sheol.

**v.25 — Yedidyah:** "Beloved of YHWH" (*yedid-Yah*). This name, given through Nathan, signals divine favor for Solomon despite the circumstances of his parents' union. The name is never used again in the text; Solomon prevails.

**v.30 — malkam:** The MT can be read as "their king" (*malkam*) or as the Ammonite deity "Milcom" (*Milkom*). If the latter, David removes the crown from an idol's head — a polemical act. The Leningrad Codex vocalization supports "their king."

**v.31 — bammegerah... bammalben:** This verse describes either forced labor (putting captives to work at saws, threshing sledges, axes, and brick-kilns) or execution by these instruments. The Hebrew is ambiguous. I follow the MT vocalization *vayasem* ("he set/placed"), which more naturally reads as forced labor, though *vayasar* ("he sawed") is an ancient variant.

*— EMET*
